Calling `await cua.getState()` returns no app/browser inventory or screenshot; the runtime reports `kernel_status: exited(code=1)` (one recorded kernel PID: 10588).

Separately, neither the dot's main task nor its delegated Windows task exposes the callable native `node_repl` tool required by the installed Windows Computer Use skill. Therefore `@oai/sky` import and `sky.list_apps()` could not run in those tasks. This is an unavailable-tool result, not evidence that Sky itself failed.

## Environment / scope

- Windows Store app package: `OpenAI.Codex`, `26.1013.3656.0`, x64. Independently rechecked in the working local chat with Get-AppxPackage on October 16, 2026.
- Windows: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64`; delegated shell also reported Windows_NT / AMD64.
- Bundled Windows Computer Use skill version used locally: `26.1013.31256`.
- Computer use > Any App was enabled in the user's screenshot.
- Main dot task: cloud Linux workspace. Its CUA surface describes that Linux desktop, not the connected Windows PC.
- Delegated task: reaches the Windows PC for shell diagnostics, but native UI tool provisioning differs from the local chat.
- Subscription: Pro (as entered in the earlier report from this account).

## Controlled comparison on the same PC

| Route | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary local Windows chat: native node_repl + @oai/sky | Successfully enumerated Windows apps/windows, launched PowerPoint and read its Home screen; later controlled Edge to create GitHub issue #54698. A later read-only sky.list_windows() returned 25 windows. |
| Dot-delegated Windows task: cua.getState() | MXC initialization fails with the exact SystemDrive error before inventory/screen capture; exit code 1. Repeated in fresh delegated tasks after reconnection and after the direct-chat repair. |
| Dot-delegated Windows task: requested native Sky test | Callable node_repl absent. Import and sky.list_apps() remain untested. |
| Dot main task | No separately callable node_repl; available CUA targets the cloud Linux workspace. It was not used as a substitute Windows test. |
| Ordinary local chat: separate cua.getState() route | Returned apps: [] plus in-app/MCP browser surfaces, without reproducing the exact delegated MXC error. This does not negate the successful native Sky route. |

## SystemDrive is present in the independently checked shells

Delegated Windows shell diagnostics reported:

```text
SystemDrive=C:
SystemRoot=C:\WINDOWS
```

The working local shell independently reported the same values. These checks do not inspect the failing MXC/viewer host process environment. They therefore neither explain where the value is lost nor prove that a Windows-wide variable is missing.

A delegated diagnostic also observed LOCALAPPDATA redirected to a path shaped like `...\Packages\sandbox.{GUID}\AC`, with the GUID differing between calls. That environment difference is relevant for investigation, but is not a demonstrated cause of the MXC error.

## Tool-availability checks reported in the supplied diagnostic transcript

- The Windows delegated task read the installed Computer Use SKILL.md, which requires node_repl initialization of @oai/sky.
- It searched a 325-entry tool catalog for node_repl, node repl, @oai/sky and sky.list_apps(): zero matches; no separately exposed discovery tool was reported.
- Main dot task separately inspected its 344-entry catalog. Only mcp__cua_repl__js matched through references in its description; no separate callable node_repl was available. CUA js/js_reset were present, targeting Linux.
- No supported task option was found to select the native Windows binding or change the CUA backend.

These catalog counts and delegated outcomes are task-reported evidence from the supplied chronology, not independently re-enumerated by this local chat.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Minimal observed workflow

1. On the connected Windows PC, enable the bundled Computer Use plugin / Any App control.
2. From a dot, request a read-only Windows test: list open Windows apps and capture one screenshot of GitHub Desktop, with no clicking or typing.
3. Have the dot create a task on the connected Windows computer.
4. In that task, call `await cua.getState()`.
5. Observe MXC preparation fail with the nonempty Unicode host SystemDrive error and kernel exit code 1, before any inventory or screenshot.
6. In a separate shell on that Windows task, check SystemDrive / SystemRoot: valid values are reported.
7. Request the alternative explicitly specified by the installed Windows skill: import @oai/sky through node_repl, then call sky.list_apps(). The required callable node_repl is absent, so this test cannot execute.
8. Check the dot's main task separately: it also lacks callable node_repl, while its CUA surface describes a Linux cloud desktop rather than this Windows PC.
9. Compare with an ordinary local chat on the same PC: the native Windows node_repl / @oai/sky path successfully lists windows and controls Windows apps.

This reproduces on the affected installation/task routes. A clean/default installation reproduction has not been established; the machine has prior troubleshooting changes documented below.

## Chronology (October 16, 2026; UTC, local offset UTC-07:00)

- 17:48-17:50: original delegated attempt could not begin the requested GitHub Desktop operation. Native node_repl was absent; the alternative MXC route failed, including after one reset. No app inventory/screenshot was returned.
- Approximately 17:53-17:58: Any App permission and valid Windows shell SystemDrive/SystemRoot were checked.
- Approximately 18:03-18:59: additional task attempts. One separate conversation reported app-server program not found; reports also described MXC failures and, in a different attempt, browser-only discovery. These are not assumed to share a backend or root cause.
- Approximately 19:12-19:28: user pursued a deep uninstall/profile reset and reported a reboot in another conversation. This changed installation state but did not establish a fix for the dot route.
- Direct local chat later repaired a separate missing code-mode-host path and successfully controlled PowerPoint/Edge. Exact per-message timestamps are unavailable in the supplied transcript.
- Approximately 20:28-20:31: fresh dot-side verification after reconnection still failed with the exact MXC SystemDrive error. Separate Windows shell values remained valid.
- Subsequent delegated check verified the repaired host link and matching hashes, but still lacked native node_repl for the requested Sky test.
- 20:38:54: main dot task separately confirmed its missing node_repl and Linux-targeted CUA surface. No main-task Windows-control call was made.

Times and delegated results above come from a compiled chronology, not a complete raw tool-log export.

### What is the expected behavior?

The dot-to-Windows route should expose a supported control tool for the connected, authorized Windows computer and initialize it successfully, or clearly explain the supported capability limit before attempting the operation.

If the Windows skill requires node_repl / @oai/sky, the tool provisioning and skill instructions should agree. A Linux cloud control surface should not be mistaken for Windows desktop control.

MXC diagnostics should identify which process/environment lacks the required variable and distinguish it from a separately functioning Windows shell. Please provide a supported fix or precise, sanitized diagnostics to identify the failing launch boundary.

### Additional information

## Separate companion-executable issue, repaired locally

Previously, ordinary local tools failed with:

```text
failed to spawn code-mode host
%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex-code-mode-host.exe:
The system cannot find the file specified. (os error 2)
```

The host existed under `bin\e78bad9887fa50cf\`, not directly under bin. The running app-server used the parent bin\codex.exe with `-c features.code_mode_host=true app-server`. Parent/version-folder codex.exe hashes matched. A later local check found CODEX_CLI_PATH set at user and process scope to the parent bin\codex.exe (origin unknown; removing it has not been tested).

The user created a hard link from the expected parent host path to that installed version-folder host. This restored local terminal execution and native Windows control. The delegated diagnostic independently verified both host paths as HardLink, size 74,921,776 bytes, with matching SHA-256:

```text
B1B21C0DC7F2CB72D27970479403AE8A10FEF6EF4AF417FE7FE9F960F8C2755A
```

Matching codex.exe SHA-256:

```text
9ECB9DF2ECAFCC00542EF0966C6F1737A81397DC9531B0A4B178238E2BF4A46D
```

This repair is documented in #54698 (related to #47432). It did NOT resolve the dot-delegated MXC error or make node_repl available to dot tasks. The hard link is a local workaround, not a confirmed permanent fix or a recommendation for other installations.

## Other distinct messages / diagnostic limits

- A separate conversation reported `failed to launch codex app-server: program not found` around 18:18 UTC. No shared cause with MXC has been proven.
- Delegated app/update checker: `App updates are only available on the local desktop host.`
- Delegated package query: `Get-AppxPackage: Access is denied.` It was stopped without escalation. Package version above was independently verified from the working local chat instead.
- One direct-chat browser attempt stopped because the controller could not reliably determine the current browser URL for policy checks. A later attempt succeeded and created #54698. This was not a persistent desktop initialization failure.
- Duplicate/stale computer connections were reported after reconnection; they have not been established as the cause or confirmed removed.
- No Windows environment/security setting, credential, or connection configuration was changed during the dot diagnostics. Broader prior troubleshooting included reinstall/profile reset and the explicit hard-link repair. It should not be described as an untouched installation.

## Open questions for maintainers

1. Is native Windows control intended to be available in dot-delegated tasks, and which runtime/tool should those tasks receive?
2. Why do the installed skill and callable tool catalog disagree?
3. Which environment is used by the failing MXC launcher, and where is SystemDrive obtained/filtered/converted?
4. Does the observed sandbox LOCALAPPDATA redirection matter for this launch boundary?
5. Are tool provisioning, environment propagation and the separate companion-host lookup independent defects? Current evidence does not establish a shared cause.
6. What supported desktop/controller fix and verification procedure applies to this route?

## Related reports

- #54477: dot-to-Windows startup reports involving SystemDrive and a working local-route comparison.
- #54648: Windows dot browser-only CUA / startup failures.
- #51927 and #49458: delegated/native-tool availability differences.
- #54698: this user's separately repaired companion-host lookup issue; linked here for context, not as the same confirmed root cause.

## Evidence provenance

Prepared from the user's supplied computer-use-diagnostic-transcript.md, relevant screenshots and the direct local troubleshooting session. The supplied document is a compiled chronology with marked quotations, not a complete verbatim tool-log export; screenshot gaps were not reconstructed. This local chat independently verified the Store package version, Windows shell values and successful native Windows control. Delegated catalog inventories, times, sandbox-path observations and failures are attributed to the supplied task reports.

Private usernames/hostname, unrelated app/project contents and account identifiers are omitted. Opaque task/turn reference IDs are retained in the original diagnostic transcript and can be provided privately to support if needed. No full raw transcript or unrelated screenshots are uploaded.

Submitted using the Computer Use plugin at the account owner's request.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1 (interactive TUI sessions); the background `codex app-server` managed daemon is 0.163.0.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 5x (`plan_type: "prolite"` in every `rate_limits` event, unchanged before and after the jump). Subscription renews 2026-11-10, no plan change this week.

### Which model were you using?

`gpt-6.1-sol` (xhigh) and `gpt-6-astra` (xhigh), `service_tier = "fast"` in config.toml.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Sessions run inside a terminal multiplexer; not relevant to the issue.

### Codex doctor report

Not run; the issue is account-side usage accounting.

### What issue are you seeing?

The weekly usage limit went from **24% used to 96% used within one hour, while no client sent any turns**. All times UTC.

Weekly window: `window_minutes: 10080`, `resets_at: 1792649598` (2026-10-22T06:13:18Z). Credits unchanged across the jump (`has_credits: true`, same balance before and after).

**Last reading before the jump** (`token_count` event, thread `01a14476-be99-7412-a372-95e66994eb14`):

```
2026-10-16T18:08:10Z  primary.used_percent = 24.0, plan_type = "prolite"
```

**First reading after the jump** (next thread, `01a14619-7b22-7cd2-899c-c76684c8bd77`, first turn):

```
2026-10-16T19:04:03Z  primary.used_percent = 96.0, plan_type = "prolite"
```

**The silent window 18:08:10Z → 19:03:57Z:**

- `state_5.sqlite` `threads`: no thread was created or updated in that window (the two threads above end at 18:08:10Z and start at 19:03:57Z).
- `logs_2.sqlite`: the only entries in that window are `app-server request: account/rateLimits/read` every ~15 s (a usage monitor polling) and their HTTP client setup lines. No `turn_input`, no model requests.
- No other Codex home or rollout files were written in that window, and no Codex cloud task activity is logged.
- A usage monitor that records the weekly percentage hourly shows: 16:56Z 23%, 17:56Z 24%, **18:56Z 96%**, 19:56Z 98%.

For scale: all local usage on 16 Oct before the jump (about ten CLI sessions over ~8 hours) moved the weekly meter from 8% to 24%.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Not reproducible on demand. Thread ids above bracket the window; I can share redacted rollout excerpts if useful.

### What is the expected behavior?

The weekly meter only increases when the account actually uses Codex. If usage was backfilled or re-attributed server-side, the usage dashboard should show where it came from, and the limit should be corrected if it is an accounting error.

### Additional information

Possibly related: #52039 (usage backfilled in analytics) and the closed #39167 (similar jump, which turned out to be a plan downgrade). In this case the plan type did not change.

items.title: Messages on Mac: persistent switch to SMS after the assistant sends a message, even though the tool returns RCS

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
Résumé
Après un envoi de texte par le plugin natif Messages, une conversation directe apparaît en mode « Message texte • SMS » sur le Mac. Le résultat de send_message et la recherche du même fil indiquent pourtant RCS. Selon l’utilisateur, le phénomène survient uniquement après les envois de l’assistant, se répète depuis plusieurs semaines et disparaît après un message entrant du correspondant. Le problème n’a pas été reproduit dans un essai contrôlé pendant cet audit.

Environnement vérifié le 16 octobre 2026
- macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434, architecture arm64.
- Application ChatGPT/Codex : 26.1013.31256, build 20586 ; identifiant com.openai.codex.
- Plugin officiel messages@openai-bundled : 1.0.1001501, activé.
- Composant Codex Computer Use : 26.1013.1001501, build 1001501.
- Aucun remplacement du serveur Messages dans la configuration MCP inspectée.
- Le contrôle softwareupdate --list s’est terminé avec « No new software available ». Cette observation concerne les mises à jour proposées par macOS, pas celles de l’application OpenAI.
- Version iOS et opérateur non relevés.

Éléments directement vérifiés
1. Le destinataire et le fil direct existant ont été identifiés avec find_chats ; le service renvoyé est RCS.
2. Un seul texte autorisé a été envoyé avec send_message, en fournissant le chat_guid existant et le texte. Aucun paramètre de canal n’a été ajouté.
3. Le résultat d’envoi indique destination_kind=existing_chat et service=RCS ; le participant est également marqué RCS.
4. La relecture du même fil retrouve le texte envoyé. Les données de relecture exposées ne fournissent ni le transport ni un accusé de livraison par message.
5. Une capture fournie par l’utilisateur montre le champ de saisie « Message texte • SMS » sur le Mac et le dernier message marqué « Distribué ». Ce dernier message ne porte pas séparément la mention « Envoyé par SMS » : la capture ne suffit donc pas à établir son transport exact. Un message antérieur porte explicitement cette mention.
6. La recherche native du même fil continue de renvoyer RCS malgré le mode SMS montré sur le Mac.

Éléments rapportés par l’utilisateur
- Le correspondant a reçu le message.
- Le même fil affiche RCS sur l’iPhone.
- Le Mac est activé dans Transfert de SMS sur l’iPhone.
- Quitter puis rouvrir Messages ne rétablit pas le mode RCS sur le Mac.
- Les bascules n’ont été constatées qu’après les envois par l’assistant.
- La réception d’un message du correspondant rétablit le RCS, sans empêcher les récidives ultérieures.

Diagnostic provisoire et limites
La différence rapportée entre envoi manuel et envoi par l’assistant oriente vers le chemin d’envoi automatisé : intégration OpenAI ou interaction avec les interfaces Apple. Elle ne permet pas d’attribuer définitivement le défaut à l’un des deux composants. Le retour service=RCS ne suffit pas ici à certifier le transport effectif du message individuel. Aucun correctif durable ni réglage documenté permettant d’imposer le RCS n’a été identifié dans les capacités exposées et les sources consultées.

Demande à l’équipe
- Reproduire un envoi vers un fil RCS existant avec le chemin chat_guid et comparer l’état du fil avant et après avec un envoi manuel.
- Préciser l’origine du champ service dans le résultat d’envoi : capacité du correspondant, métadonnée du fil ou transport réellement utilisé par ce message.
- Examiner pourquoi un message entrant rétablit le mode RCS après cette bascule.
- Fournir un correctif ou un contournement pris en charge, et rendre explicite tout repli réel vers SMS dans le résultat d’envoi.

Audit effectué sans nouvel envoi de test, suppression de conversation, réinitialisation, modification du plugin ni changement des réglages Apple.

Sources officielles consultées
- OpenAI, utilisation du plugin Apple Messages : https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/plugins#use-apple-messages-from-codex
- Apple, transfert des SMS/MMS/RCS vers les autres appareils : https://support.apple.com/fr-fr/102545
- Apple, service RCS : https://support.apple.com/fr-fr/122195
